item.title: Queen Latifah & The Roots Join 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Queen Latifah adds a Thanksgiving TV date as The Roots, Keke Palmer and Wyclef Jean join Macy's milestone celebration.
item.content:encoded:
Queen Latifah is heading into Thanksgiving with another national television appearance, joining the performers announced for the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade. The November 26 event will also feature The Roots with Jimmy Fallon, Keke Palmer and Wyclef Jean.

The lineup arrived Friday, ahead of a milestone broadcast that brings several generations of entertainers to New York. Viewers can watch on NBC, Peacock and Telemundo beginning at 8:30 A.M. ET.

“We’re creating a celebration of unprecedented scale and will deliver an unforgettable Thanksgiving for millions across the country,” Macy’s chief marketing officer Sharon Otterman said.

The parade will follow another major career honor for Latifah: her November 14 induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Her television schedule has expanded, too, after she joined The Voice as a coach for its 30th season alongside Kelly Clarkson, Adam Levine and Riley Green.

That range stretches back decades, from the demo that brought her a Tommy Boy deal in 1988 to her work on Living Single and in Set It Off. The Rock Hall recognition follows a BET Lifetime Achievement Award in 2021 and the addition of her debut album to the National Recording Registry in 2023, a first for a female rapper.

“Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade brings the extraordinary together: iconic entertainers and emerging talent, artistry and imagination, hometown pride, cherished traditions and the thrill of discovering something new,” Otterman added.

The holiday lineup also includes JoJo, Natalie Merchant, DEVO, Anthony Ramos, Leslie Odom Jr. and the Indigo Girls. Teddy Swims and Megan Moroney are scheduled to perform in front of Macy’s 34th Street flagship, while other performers will travel along the route on floats.

Macy’s first staged the parade in 1924, but the event was interrupted for three years during World War II. The centennial edition will feature 100 inflatable elements along the route.

EJAE and RIIZE bring K-pop representation to the broadcast, with Feid and Icona Pop also included in the announced roster. Savannah Guthrie, Hoda Kotb and Al Roker will host, and organizers have more performers and Broadway participants left to announce.

Megan Hilty will lead a tribute to Dolly Parton during the parade.

item.title: Grammys Move Most Award Presentations To Disney+ For 2027
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Grammys send their trophy-heavy Premiere Ceremony to Disney+ as Fulwell takes over production ahead of the ABC debut.
item.content:encoded:
The Grammys are moving the ceremony that hands out most of their trophies to Disney+ in 2027. The Premiere Ceremony will stream exclusively on the service, starting February 7 at 2:30 P.M. Eastern.

Kendrick Lamar‘s 2025 sweep showed how much can happen before the prime-time cameras come on. “Not Like Us” collected Best Rap Performance, Best Rap Song and Best Music Video during the earlier ceremony.

About 90 of the show’s 100 awards are presented at Premiere, according to Billboard. The event previously streamed through the Grammys website and will return to Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater.

Recording Academy CEO Harvey Mason Jr. welcomed the change in a statement reported by Billboard. “The Premiere Ceremony has always been one of the most celebratory moments of Grammy Sunday,” he said.

“With the ceremony streaming on Disney+ for the first time, even more fans will get to be part of that celebration. To bring it to life for a new audience, we couldn’t ask for a better partner than Fulwell, and I’m confident they’ll bring the same magic they bring to the telecast year after year,” Mason continued.

Fulwell Entertainment is taking over production of Premiere for the first time after years of producing the main broadcast. Ben Winston, Eric Pankowski and Greg V. Fera will serve as its executive producers.

Mustard accepted Lamar’s three early trophies in 2025, before “Not Like Us” added Record and Song of the Year. The Academy’s official video captures the Best Rap Performance acceptance.

The 2027 ballot also introduces Best R&B Collaboration or Duo/Group Performance. That addition comes alongside renaming Best R&B Performance to Best R&B Solo Performance.

Disney’s agreement with the Recording Academy runs through 2036, covering a decade of broadcasts. ABC takes over after CBS carried the awards annually from 1973 through 2026.

Nominees in all 100 categories will be announced November 16, starting at 7:45 A.M. Eastern on Grammy.com and YouTube. Kehlani, Pharrell Williams, Olivia Dean and Herbie Hancock are among the presenters.

The main awards show begins February 7 at 7 P.M. Eastern from Crypto.com Arena and will be simulcast on ABC, Disney+, and Hulu.

item.title: Damon Dash Ordered To Turn Over Pricey Andy Warhol Painting In Bankruptcy
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Dame Dash's bankruptcy trustee targets a Warhol print and three more works while challenging his family ownership claims.
item.content:encoded:
Dame Dash faces a demand to surrender four artworks his bankruptcy trustee values above $225,000, as she seeks another source of money for creditors. The request includes an Andy Warhol print and a possible role for U.S. Marshals if he defies a future turnover order.

Trustee Traci K. Stevenson filed the motion November 12 in Florida bankruptcy court. She wants Dash to deliver the pieces and ownership records within seven days after a judge grants the request.

Stevenson estimates Warhol’s “Geronimo” alone could bring more than $100,000. Her list also includes Mr. Brainwash’s “Obama Superman” at $35,000, Peter Beard’s “Giraffes in Mirage” at $40,000 and Donald Baechler’s “Beachball” at $50,000.

The ownership dispute runs through Dash’s March 5 questioning under oath, which the motion quotes. Asked whether the Warhol was in his home, Dash answered, “I don’t have — it’s not in my home.”

Asked whether it was on the property where he lived, Dash replied, “Yeah.” He described it as being “in the family office” and said, “whenever we do art and we have art, it all goes to my kids.”

Stevenson says Dash never identified that office’s owners or supplied documents establishing a transfer. She also alleges he left valuable artwork off his bankruptcy disclosures and produced no authentication certificates or purchase records after her request.

Asked about insurance during the same examination, Dash said, “No. It’s not insurable.” Stevenson proposes moving the works into insured, climate-controlled storage.

Dash’s art ventures stretch back to The Dash Gallery, which opened in 2010. The motion also cites his testimony that he held a 50% stake in Poppington with Raquel Horn.

The demand follows the court-approved $550,000 sale of his life rights and Roc-A-Fella archives to Everlasting Films. That transaction covers his life through September 4, 2025, when he filed Chapter 7.

For the artwork, Stevenson seeks permission to inspect and remove the pieces with fine-art handlers after 48 hours’ notice. She also wants an order preventing their sale, movement or concealment while turnover remains pending.

Stevenson plans to seek separate court approval before hiring an appraiser or auctioneer to market the collection.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Nicki Minaj’s History With Past Lawyers Comes Back To Haunt Her In $275K Lawsuit
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Nicki Minaj's production-company opponent cites past lawyer disputes as it seeks to limit delays in her $275,000 lawsuit.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj‘s troubles keeping lawyers are now ammunition for the production company suing her for $275,149.62, which wants her latest legal breakup to stop costing it time.

In a court filing obtained by AllHipHop, 24/7 Productions attorney Joshua B. Katz said the company won’t fight her lawyers’ exit. But it wants a New York judge to require replacement counsel promptly, citing her history of defaults and fractured attorney relationships.

“Defendants should not receive additional time because their relationship with their own counsel has broken down,” Katz wrote.

The McLaughlin & Stern lawyer continued: “A protracted delay while Defendants seek and retain new counsel would shift the cost of that breakdown to 24/7 and extend a delay that has already kept 24/7 from payment for services it rendered and out-of-pocket costs it incurred nearly three years ago.”

Kurzman Eisenberg Corbin & Lever represents Minaj and Pink Friday Productions LLC. Katz’s affirmation quotes the firm’s withdrawal papers describing “Irreconcilable differences” over representation, disagreements about litigation strategy and a communication breakdown.

To explain his concern, Katz pointed to earlier turmoil in Tameer Peak’s lawsuit against Minaj. His filing recounts a missed response deadline, a clerk’s default and successive lawyers’ departures, relying on published reporting about that case.

He also cited former firm Gordon Rees Scully Mansukhani’s unpaid-fee lawsuit and the default judgment obtained by security guard Thomas Weidenmuller. Katz presented those episodes as reasons not to give Minaj an open-ended pause while she finds another legal team.

The 24/7 lawsuit began March 23, 2026. The company says it supplied live-event production and support for December 2023 iHeartRadio Jingle Ball shows in Chicago and Atlanta, plus New York promotional events for Pink Friday 2.

Its demand includes $255,149.62 in out-of-pocket expenses, it says, that it advanced for the defendants. Minaj’s defense has disputed the debt, arguing Pink Friday Productions paid the bills and that ownership alone doesn’t make her personally liable.

AllHipHop previously reported that Judge Leslie A. Stroth paused proceedings and scheduled a December 1 hearing on the withdrawal request. The order contemplated another 30 days to secure counsel, or a different period set by the court.

Katz argues an automatic stay doesn’t apply to this voluntary withdrawal and is asking the judge to limit any further delay. His November 12 affirmation is filed as NYSCEF Document 38 in case 651775/2026.

Replies on the withdrawal motion are due November 23, ahead of the December hearing.

item.title: B2K’s Label Reports 138,000 Ticket-And-Album Bundles For ECLIPSE
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: B2K's comeback reaches beyond streaming as its label reports 138,000 packages pairing ECLIPSE with reunion tour tickets.
item.content:encoded:
B2K‘s reunion tour helped sell its new music before listeners ever pressed play on ECLIPSE.

The group’s label now reports 138,000 ticket-and-album bundles, putting a concrete number behind a comeback built around concertgoers rather than streaming alone.

BPC Music Group disclosed the figure Thursday in its announcement about the campaign with Black Promoters Collective. The total describes packages combining the album and Boys 4 Life Tour tickets, not a separately reported first-week album sales tally.

“The Boys 4 Life Tour gave us a way to make that music part of an experience fans were already excited about,” BPC Music Group co-founder Troy Brown said in the supplied statement. ECLIPSE was the label’s first album release.

That connection is visible on B2K’s own website, where the album is offered through a redemption process reserved for concert ticket holders. Buyers are directed to enter a code delivered by email rather than purchase the project again through that page.

The site lists 12 tracks, including “Today,” “Vibrate” and “I’m Outside,” with Bow Wow appearing on “Boyfriend.” A separate Apple Music listing dates the album’s release to November 6 and gives its running time as 40 minutes.

The return to studio recording after nearly 24 years brought Raz-B, Lil’ Fizz, Omarion and J-Boog back together. Their previous studio album, Pandemonium!, arrived in 2002, while the new sessions included contributions from Hitmaka, Sean Garrett and The Underdogs.

B2K has also built a place to reach listeners without relying entirely on streaming playlists. Its EVEN STUDIO-powered online hub has hosted livestreams and a group chat, making the website part of the reunion beyond the album download itself.

The platform also gives the group information about who participates, helping it understand the audience gathering around the project and future releases.

For BPC, the reported bundle count gives the company a measure of that audience’s purchasing activity. The announcement does not provide a separate total for completed album redemptions or say how many of the packages qualified for Billboard’s charts.

B2K performed new songs and familiar hits on NBC’s TODAY on November 4, two days before the streaming release.

item.title: Whitney Houston Discoverer Gerry Griffith Dies At 87
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Gerry Griffith's death puts a spotlight on the record executive who helped launch Whitney Houston's extraordinary career.
item.content:encoded:
Whitney Houston was still a teenager singing alongside her mother when Gerry Griffith heard the voice that would transform Arista Records. The executive who helped put her in front of Clive Davis has died at 87.

Griffith died November 5 in Brooklyn after living with dementia for five years, according to Billboard. His career stretched beyond Houston to work with Aretha Franklin, Dionne Warwick and Carlos Santana.

That Houston connection wasn’t a single lucky introduction. Griffith first heard the 16-year-old perform with Cissy Houston in 1979, then returned to hear her in 1983. With another label reportedly interested, he persuaded Davis to attend a showcase before Arista signed her.

“It takes more than just talent, and that’s what Whitney had at such a young age. Besides the voice, with its range, tone and emotion, she displayed a fearless confidence and stage presence,” Griffith told Billboard in 2012.

The signing opened a two-year runway to Houston’s 1985 debut. “Saving All My Love For You,” “How Will I Know” and “Greatest Love Of All” became consecutive No. 1 singles, turning that early conviction into a historic launch. Her follow-up, Whitney, entered the album chart at No. 1 in 1987, a first for a woman, and extended her streak of chart-topping singles.

Manager and publisher Deirdre O’Hara remembered her own place in that chain of introductions.

“Early in my music publishing career, I was very fortunate to connect with Gerry. One of my proudest moments was urging him to see Whitney Houston, and he subsequently brought Clive Davis to see her. The rest is history,” O’Hara said.

Griffith’s work also reached The Bodyguard soundtrack, extending his connection to Houston into her movie career. The album won the Grammy for album of the year and later joined her debut among the records that returned to the Top 10 after her death.

The Chicago native served in the Army before entering music. At EMI’s Manhattan Records, he worked with Richard Marx, while his broader credits included Santana’s Supernatural era and the Pretty Woman soundtrack.

Griffith’s survivors include two daughters and two sons, with a memorial service planned for a later date.

item.title: Suno Faces Bigger Reservoir Lawsuit As AI Claims Top $445 Million
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Suno's Reservoir case grows to 1,368 songs as the publisher raises its demands against two AI companies to $445 million.
item.content:encoded:
Suno’s fight with Reservoir now covers hundreds more songs, pushing the publisher’s combined demands against the AI music company and Anthropic above $445 million. The catalog at issue includes music recorded by Madonna, Joni Mitchell and Miles Davis.

Reservoir filed amended complaints in Northern California federal court on November 11. Its revised Suno complaint identifies 1,368 compositions, while the separate Anthropic action covers 1,143 works.

Those totals increase the lists from 1,050 and 853 songs, respectively. Reservoir is asking for as much as $205.2 million in copyright damages from Suno and $171.45 million from Anthropic, before its additional claims over access controls and copyright information.

Adding the amounts requested across all three claims in both lawsuits brings the total to $445,702,500. That is Reservoir’s demand, not money a judge has awarded.

The extra demands total $37.62 million against Suno and $31.43 million against Anthropic. They concern allegations that the companies bypassed protections on source material and removed copyright-management information, including details identifying songwriters and publishers.

The Suno filing keeps a detail familiar to anyone who listens to rap: producer tags. Reservoir alleges that generated tracks reproduce those recognizable signatures, part of the producer-tag dispute AllHipHop previously covered.

“For example, Suno has output ‘producer tags’ which are an integral musical part of songs throughout the hip-hop and rap genres, and function as a type of signature for a producer,” Reservoir alleges in the amended complaint.

The publisher also points to 34 recorded examples it says demonstrate copied musical material. Its claims go beyond what listeners hear: Reservoir accuses Suno of obtaining protected music without permission and stripping information that identifies its creators and owners.

Anthropic faces a different output complaint centered on Claude. Reservoir alleges that the chatbot reproduces lyrics and makes adaptations using its compositions, and claims it copied material during training and retains it for future use.

Both filings seek orders to stop the alleged infringement and require unauthorized copies to be impounded or destroyed. Reservoir also wants an accounting of the companies’ training data and scraping activities involving its music.

Reservoir Media Management, its UK affiliate and Shapiro, Bernstein & Co. Limited are the plaintiffs in both cases.

item.title: Yella Beezy Mugshot After Life Sentence Has People Doing Double Takes
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Yella Beezy begins serving his life sentence as Texas officials release another booking photo after the Dallas murder trial.
item.content:encoded:
Yella Beezy has been transferred to a Texas prison following his conviction in MO3’s killing, with a new booking photograph released Friday.

The move comes two days after a Dallas jury found him guilty of capital murder and he received life without parole.

The new image was released by Texas prison officials after the rapper’s transfer, TMZ reported November 13.

He had been taken into Dallas County custody following Wednesday’s verdict.

His defense team has already said it intends to challenge the conviction. Attorney Toby Shook disputed the prosecution’s case after the verdict and announced plans for an appeal.

“We’re going to keep fighting. We have excellent appellate points and that will be the next step in the fight,” Shook said after the verdict.

The jury’s decision arrived on the sixth anniversary of MO3’s death. The Dallas County District Attorney’s Office said the conviction held Yella Beezy responsible for arranging and financing the November 11, 2020, attack.

MO3 was driving on Interstate 35E in Dallas when an armed man approached. He left his vehicle and ran, but the gunman chased him and opened fire on the highway.

Prosecutors argued that the shooting grew out of a feud between the two rappers.

Yella Beezy pleaded not guilty and denied hiring the gunman, while his attorneys challenged the financial evidence and witness accounts presented at trial.

Among those disputes was a $40,000 cash withdrawal made nine days after the killing. During cross-examination, the defense pressed investigators about their inability to trace recovered money directly to that transaction.

The defense also questioned an alleged confession at a South Dallas barbershop. Cell-tower analysis placed Yella Beezy’s phone in Frisco, and investigators acknowledged they lacked corroborating evidence placing him at the shop.

Before reaching their verdict, jurors requested rap lyrics, FBI reports and financial statements for further review during deliberations.

They ultimately returned a unanimous decision against the Dallas rapper.

Gunman Kewon White was convicted of capital murder in September and also received life without parole.

Another defendant, Devin Brown, still faces a capital murder charge and is awaiting trial.

A bystander wounded during the highway shooting survived.

item.title: MC Lyte Lines Up New Sitcom And 2027 Movies Before Rock Hall Induction
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: MC Lyte adds acting, directing and a film slate to her next chapter as she prepares to enter the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame.
item.content:encoded:
MC Lyte has a sitcom on her schedule and movies lined up for production in 2027, giving her Rock & Roll Hall of Fame moment a decidedly forward-looking twist.

The rapper is preparing to work behind and in front of the camera rather than simply collect another career honor.

“Our company is co-executive-producing a new sitcom. I’m acting and directing in it,” Lyte said in a new Billboard interview.

She also revealed that she filmed a YouTube series with VanVan in Charlotte, North Carolina, although she didn’t supply titles or release dates for those projects.

Those details give shape to plans she had only hinted at publicly. In September, Lyte told AllHipHop she had acting and directing work coming as she returned to the studio with Warryn Campbell, the producer behind her 2024 album, 1 of 1.

“There’s some acting stuff coming up,” Lyte told AllHipHop’s Chuck “Jigsaw” Creekmur in that conversation, which also touched on her directing work. “So I’m just excited.” Discussing her client projects as well, she added, “We are just overflowing with things to do. So, the to-do list is long, Chuck.”

The screen work isn’t a sudden detour. Lyte previously played Detective Monroe in the BET+ series Angel, and she discussed her growing enthusiasm for directing with AllHipHop in 2024 after making the short film Break Up in Love.

That earlier television role put her in a crime drama, a different format from the sitcom she is now planning to help produce.

Her relationship with VanVan also predates the newly disclosed series.

The young rapper joined her Sunni Gyrl roster, and the two participated in the Kennedy Center’s 2023 tribute to Queen Latifah, connecting Lyte’s mentorship work with another woman whose career moved between records and Hollywood.

Building those ventures has meant learning more than how to deliver a verse.

Looking back on the obstacles she faced, Lyte told Billboard, “The hardest part was just the business.” She described a learning curve that required young performers to understand the commercial side alongside their creative work.

The Hall recognition dates back to an earlier breakthrough: her 1988 debut, Lyte as a Rock, made her the first female rapper to release a full-length solo album. A year later, Eyes on This brought another milestone as the first solo album by a female rapper to enter the Billboard 200.

Lyte’s induction ceremony takes place November 14 at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater.

item.title: Kanye West’s Alice Merton Sample Case Dismissed After Settlement Deal
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Kanye West's settlement with Alice Merton removes a March trial date, while the court leaves room to reopen the case.
item.content:encoded:
Kanye West‘s sample dispute with Alice Merton has moved off the trial calendar after the two sides reached a settlement.

A federal judge dismissed the case without prejudice while leaving a 90-day window to reopen it if the deal runs into trouble.

Judge Fernando L. Aenlle-Rocha issued the dismissal order and canceled every remaining deadline. Merton and her companies had notified the court six days earlier that they had reached an agreement with Ye and Yeezy Record Label.

The November 6 notice said the settlement would resolve the entire case once its obligations were completed.

It anticipated approximately 30 to 45 days of performance after the written agreement was signed.

“Upon full performance, the Parties will file a stipulation dismissing the entire action with prejudice,” Merton’s lawyers wrote. The filing did not disclose a dollar amount or spell out those obligations.

Merton sued over “Gun To My Head,” alleging the Vultures 2 track incorporated her 2022 song “Blindside” despite her refusal to authorize it. The German singer said her family’s history as Holocaust survivors and Ye’s antisemitic statements drove that refusal.

Her complaint followed a clearance request sent to BMG in February 2024. She declined permission the following month, but alleged Ye released the song that August anyway.

The case had recently produced a ruling keeping references to antisemitism and the Holocaust in the lawsuit. Ye’s lawyers sought to remove those allegations, arguing they were unrelated to the copyright dispute.

Aenlle-Rocha rejected that request in October because the allegations helped explain Merton’s refusal. Ye’s defense also challenged the evidence supporting her infringement claim.

The new dismissal allows either side to request reopening within 90 days by explaining why settlement remains incomplete, what still needs doing and when completion is expected. The parties can instead file their agreed dismissal with prejudice within that period.

“All deadlines governing this action are VACATED,” Aenlle-Rocha wrote in the order. The settlement notice had also asked to remove a November 20 hearing on the defendants’ pending summary-judgment motion from the court’s calendar.

The now-canceled trial had been scheduled for March 15, 2027.
